summary: PICOTokens splits a claim at the first polarity-verb match that survives two skips: a match right after that/which/who/whom (its clause modifies the intervention) and a match that leaves either side without content tokens. The gate stays direction-blind; the rules decide only where the claim splits.
reason: Splitting at the first match silently disabled the gate for claims opening with a participle ('reduced sodium intake lowers blood pressure') and moved a relative clause's object onto the outcome side ('a diet that lowers cholesterol prevents heart disease').
validated_outcome: pico_split_test.go: 3 verb-first and 4 subordinate claims split as annotated; all 14 corpora keep identical token pairs and drop counts. Removing either skip fails its test; returning nil always fails 6 new and 3 cli tests; adding 'of' as a subordinator fails none.
